@seanphwang  @emikes919 sorry about this - that's a pretty bad experience. The intent with building more automated systems is to speed up approval, but it looks like maybe something went wrong here. We do regularly review automated approvals and rejections so I'm sure we'll debug this soon (and if you raised the issue, I'm sure the team is debugging our systems as well).   
  
As a general rule, if a post is an insight that's useful to the community, or a genuine question that's useful to you (that the community can help with), it's going to make a good post. [...] To be honest, the posting guideline that is provided to us is not that detailed. It leaves a ton of room for whoever reviewing to approve/reject however way they see fit.  
  
Currently, out of 10 threads I submit, only 3-4 gets approved. If anyone have experience with low approval rates and was able to improve that over time, please do share with us!

One chat to manage your inbox, calendar, tasks, contacts, and follow-ups across Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar, Drive, and LinkedIn. The core idea: nothing executes without your approval. The AI drafts emails, schedules meetings, triages your inbox, processes invoices. But every action goes through an approval queue first. You review, edit if needed, approve. results.title: Tycoon AI Competitors & Alternatives (2026) | Product Hunt
results.content:
A major advantage is its human-in-the-loop design, which makes it safer to automate expensive, risky, or brand-sensitive actions. That review-and-approve checkpoint is ideal when automation needs guardrails, and it’s often the difference between experimentation and something a team can confidently run in production.

Relay also tends to be easier to roll out to non-technical stakeholders than more developer-leaning automation stacks, with workflows that stay readable and maintainable as they grow. For organizations that want “agent-like” execution but still need control, transparency, and ownership, it offers a practical middle ground between simple zaps and complex orchestration. [...] In evaluating these options, we looked at time-to-value for non-technical teams, depth and reliability of integrations, collaboration and review/approval controls, observability and debugging at scale, pricing/credit predictability, and how well each product supports everything from solo workflows to team-wide rollout.

## Relay.app

Relay.appRelay.app

Build an AI team that works for you

5.0 · 43 reviews

Learn more →

Relay.app is a strong Tycoon AI alternative when the priority is dependable, cross-app automation rather than an “AI CEO” managing broad company initiatives. It’s built for turning repeatable operational work into clear workflows that connect tools like email, CRMs, docs, and internal systems, so teams can standardize processes instead of improvising every run. [...] If the goal is to get real workflows shipping fast—without turning automation into a dedicated engineering project—Relay.app is a compelling fit.

### Best for

Best for ops, RevOps, and GTM teams that need safe, team-friendly automations across SaaS tools.

### Standout features

 ✓Human-in-the-loop approvals
 ✓Readable, maintainable workflow builder
 ✓Strong Notion and LinkedIn integrations
 ✓Debugging and run transparency tools
